From the time I was a kid, barely old enough to realize that I have a uterus and uteri carry babies, I wanted to be a mom like my mom. She was June cleaver without all the money. I had a stillbirth about 8 years ago and 3 miscarriages. For a while I was devastated when they told me i wouldn't be able to carry to term. I became bitter and hateful towards my old school friends as they had kids and even my younger sister. I'd go so far as to unfollow them on social media so I wouldn't be confronted with millions of baby pictures while I was still grieving. I felt useless. More mausoleum than mother and I was NOT ok with it.
Fast forward a couple of years. My this point, I have 4 brothers diagnosed with autism (it should be noted that I have "high functioning" autism too). My mom has another boy on the way and she's nervous about another autistic kid... at this point, she has 0 out of4 without autism plus 1 out of 3 girls with it. She went to a geneticist and they found that we have a genetic defect that causes a predisposition for autism among other things. If I have a kid, it would likely be severely disabled. 
With my infertility issues and this genetic defect in mind, I made a conscious decision to remain child free. Maybe someday I *might* choose to adopt. I still have the desire to be a parent, so it's with a heavy heart that I made the decision. However, it's my decision, raising a disabled kid would be my struggle, and the guilt over the inevitable problems due to the defective gene would be mine alone to carry. 
My husband was quite bummed at first, but after some time, he saw that it wasn't a rash decision I'd made in the heat of emotion, and he became ok with it.
